tldr: Mastercard Agent Pay is a proprietary card-network program. Registered agents get scoped agentic tokens, sign their web requests, and can carry Verifiable Intent proof of what the user approved. Use is mixed: pilots plus early partner deployments.
whyItExists: A card network cannot tell an agent purchase from a human one, or from fraud, when the agent types a stolen-looking card number into a form. Agent Pay gives the network a way to know which agent is buying, under whose authority and within which limits: agents register and are certified, they receive tokens instead of card numbers, the tokens carry the consumer's limits, and merchants can check a signature on the agent's web request. Verifiable Intent adds a signed record of what the user approved, so issuers and merchants have evidence when a purchase is questioned.

whatItIsNot.text: Not AP2. AP2 is an open mandate protocol that Google launched and contributed to the FIDO Alliance; Agent Pay is Mastercard's card-network program. As specifications they meet only through Verifiable Intent, which reuses AP2's mandate type strings. Google's 2026-11-17 statement that Gemini buys with AP2 names Mastercard only for digital tokens on supported cards, not Agent Pay or Verifiable Intent.
Not the same thing as a Visa agentic token. Both networks use the words, but Mastercard Agentic Tokens and Visa's agentic network tokens are separate products from separate networks.
Not an open protocol. Mastercard sets the rules alone, and the Acceptance Framework specification it refers developers to is not public. Only Verifiable Intent is open.

Not at scale yet. Mastercard publishes no volume or value figures, and its CEO said on 2026-10-29 that the numbers are not yet significant (reported). Most transactions Mastercard names are pilots, controlled trials or first transactions; the live partner uses, such as Shop Pay purchases in AI agents (2026-10-28), two purchases with Verifiable Intent that Mastercard and its partners announced (2026-11-12 and 2026-11-19) and ChatGPT Wallet (2026-11-13, no Mastercard program named), are recent. Issuer enablement, which the CEO said reached nearly all Mastercards worldwide by 2026-04-30 (reported), is not use.

Not a new token platform. Agentic tokens build on Mastercard tokenization, and Mastercard's Agent Pay developer page, as read on 2026-10-21, lists network tokenization through MDES among Agent Pay's technologies.

Not a new liability regime. Mastercard says standard chargeback rights apply. Its public rules (2026-06-02 edition) point participants to Mastercard Agent Pay Program Standards that are not public; no agent-specific reason code, liability shift or interchange category is published (as of 2026-10-21).
Not a payments SDK. The Mastercard Developers Agent Toolkit is an MCP server that reads documentation and API specifications and makes no payment calls.

changedRecently.text: Mastercard announced a live coffee purchase through Antom that it says ran on Agent Pay with Verifiable Intent, and a completed Agent Pay for Machines pilot with Antom in Singapore. The release names no merchant, no market for the purchase and no party that checked the chain.

At the Singapore FinTech Festival, Rakuten Mobile signed a memorandum with Mastercard to explore integrating its Travel eSIM Platform with Agent Pay, and Yeahka said it signed an agreement under which YeahPay is to process Agent Pay transactions started in what it calls the Mastercard App (Yeahka's account, reported). Both showed demonstrations; neither gave a launch date.
Temu and Mastercard announced a memorandum of understanding under which they will explore agentic commerce through Agent Pay, with no date or market given.

Google said Gemini uses AP2 for purchases and named Mastercard and Visa, with American Express coming soon, for digital tokens on supported cards; it named no Agent Pay program and no Verifiable Intent.

ChatGPT Wallet began rolling out to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers in dots; OpenAI names no Mastercard program. As read 2026-11-21 its post names American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa as partners, where the launch-day text named three; Chase takes part as a card issuer.
Travelport, Booked AI, Basis Theory and Mastercard announced a live end-to-end flight purchase in which, they say, Verifiable Intent linked the customer's approval to the transaction.
Mastercard's CEO said a broad strategic partnership with OpenAI includes the use of Agent Pay, and called agent transaction numbers not yet significant (earnings call, reported).
Shopify said Shop Pay purchases in AI agents from merchants off Shopify use Mastercard, Visa and Discover tokens; Mastercard's CEO said the next day that Shop Pay uses Agent Pay (reported).
Mastercard opened Agent Pay for Machines Early Access with buyer- and seller-side APIs, a toolkit and a sandbox, and said AP4M builds on x402.

Mastercard named the Agent Pay Trust Framework and published its white paper, said a probability score for agent-initiated transactions is rolling out for US testing, and named Skyfire as a Know Your Agent partner.
Mastercard announced Agent Pay for Machines for high-frequency, low-value machine payments across cards, accounts and stablecoins.
Mastercard said all its European issuers are enabled for Agent Pay at network level, with 36 named banks completing controlled live transactions.
Mastercard contributed Verifiable Intent to the FIDO Alliance on the day Google contributed AP2.
Verifiable Intent pull request 23 renamed constraint keys to the mandate.payment.* form without a new version number.
Mastercard announced Verifiable Intent and opened the agent-intent/verifiable-intent repository.
Stripe extended Shared Payment Tokens to carry Mastercard agentic network tokens.
Santander and Mastercard said they completed Europe's first live end-to-end agent payment, in a controlled environment and explicitly not a commercial rollout.
